$comment: Related-concept links. Drawn as dotted connectors with the label 'Related'. They NEVER gate, recommend detours, trigger remediation, or count as prerequisites, and they are undirected. A related link may not duplicate a hard prerequisite edge between the same two chapters (validator rule). Deliberately excludes Integrals—Work, Energy and Power, and any two-way Vectors/Motion in a Plane prerequisite.

links.note: A derivative is an instantaneous rate; velocity is the rate of change of position.
Resolving a vector uses sine and cosine of its direction angle.
SHM displacement is a sinusoidal function of time.
Vector Algebra formalises the vectors first met in Motion in a Plane.
The magnetic force on a moving charge is a vector product.
Rates of change and extrema appear as velocity, acceleration and turning points of motion.
Parabolic and spherical reflecting surfaces are conic sections.
An AC generator's emf varies sinusoidally in time, like SHM displacement. Not a prerequisite: the generator needs angular velocity and the cosine of the coil angle, not SHM.
